clips.text_zh: 又有4chan仔話買金嘅人係白痴，金價根本係泡沫尾段，1980s嘅孳息已經爆上嚟。btw我CFD又輸緊，睇完好似仲灰。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Are you guys buying gold right now? That is genuinely retarded. Imagine bagholding gold as yields are blowing up back to 1980s levels. There were two years (2020 and 2021) where inflation was actually outpacing the rate hikes. In real terms, yields have been climbing every year since then.
clips.text_en_b2: Honestly, anyone piling into gold right now is asking for trouble. With yields climbing back toward 1980s levels and the metal coasting on a speculative bubble, the parallels with the 70s top are becoming uncomfortably obvious. Two years, 2020 and 2021, saw inflation outpacing rate hikes, yet real yields have trended upward ever since. What followed last time was the worst gold crash in history, followed by two decades of pain. CFD bagholders, take note: today is October 2026 and the chart still looks toppy.
clips.text_en_c1: Honestly, anybody still piling into gold right now needs to have a serious word with themselves. Yields have effectively normalised to levels last witnessed in the early 1980s, a period that should give any rational investor pause. During 2020 and 2021, headline inflation demonstrably outpaced every rate hike the Fed implemented, yet in real terms those yields have continued climbing ever since. That precedent mirrors the late 1970s precisely: gold coasting on a speculative bubble, followed by the worst crash in its history and a two-decade bear market. CFD bagholders, take note. Stack cash, not metal. Today is October 2026, and the chart remains conspicuously toppy.
clips.text_en_c2: Acquiring bullion at present strikes me as an exercise in profound folly, given that real yields are staging an inexorable march back toward the punishing territory last witnessed in the early 1980s. During 2020 and 2021, inflation demonstrably outstripped successive rate hikes, and ever since, in real terms, the yield curve has trended remorselessly upward. The historical analogue is rather instructive: gold coasted through the late seventies on residual speculative momentum from prior inflation, culminating in the most catastrophic bullion rout on record and a subsequent two-decade bear market. CFD bagholders, take heed. The prudent posture remains one of hoarding liquidity rather than a yellow rock that scarcely justifies its mystique. As of October 2026, the chart nonetheless retains a distinctly toppy character.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ anon argues against buying gold right now as yields rise

clips.text_zh: 4chan瘋狂陰謀論，話特朗普會將黃金儲備tokenize成$TRUMP，再變新美金標準。ok我信你個邪，lol。btw我futures又輸緊。
clips.text_en_b1: They are going to hyperinflate the USD. Per project 2025 and QAnon, they will introduce a new currency backed by a commodity. Trump periodically checks the gold reserves to make sure the gold is still there. Trump is now cozying up with Sergey for his tokenization tech. He will tokenize the gold reserves into $TRUMP.
clips.text_en_b2: Per QAnon and Project 2025, the plan is to hyperinflate the dollar and introduce a new commodity-backed currency alongside it. Trump allegedly keeps checking the gold reserves, while cozying up to Sergey for tokenization tech. The theory goes that reserves get tokenized into $TRUMP, backed by gold, effectively becoming a parallel gold standard. No coin required, just vibes and central planning. I am posting this on /biz/ in October 2026 so I can later claim I called it before it happened.
clips.text_en_c1: They are preparing to hyperinflate the USD into oblivion. Citing Project 2025 and assorted QAnon adjacent material, the theory runs as follows: Trump periodically inspects the gold reserves to verify their continued existence, has cozied up to Sergey for tokenisation infrastructure, and intends to mint a $TRUMP token fully collateralised by those reserves. That token would then constitute a parallel gold standard, effectively a second national currency alongside a deliberately debased dollar. No physical coin required, only vibes and central planning. Posting this on /biz/ in October 2026 so that, should it transpire, I can credibly claim I called it.
clips.text_en_c2: The prevailing conspiratorial fever on /biz/ holds that the administration will deliberately hyperinflate the greenback before unveiling a tokenised, commodity-backed successor currency. Drawing selectively upon Project 2025 and the more florid reaches of QAnon mythology, proponents contend that Trump periodically inspects Fort Knox to confirm the reserves remain physically extant, and that his recent rapprochement with Sergey is predicated on acquiring the requisite tokenisation infrastructure. The bullion, once transmuted into $TRUMP, would ostensibly underwrite a parallel gold standard operating alongside a debased dollar. No minting required, merely vibes and a rather audacious exercise in central planning. I am memorialising this on /biz/ in October 2026, several months before it inevitably comes to pass, so posterity may recognise prescience.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ conspiracy about $TRUMP token being backed by US gold

clips.text_zh: 睇完好驚。一個老細用兩個Claude Max plan build咗成個product，年賺過百萬美金USD，零code。我哋打工程嘅遲早畀AI取代。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Is everyone just bad at using AI? What is the deal with everyone saying that AI produces slop code? I work for a very profitable small software company in the US. I have built systems with throughputs of hundreds of millions of dollars in transactions a year, netting over 14 million dollars a month in profit.
clips.text_en_b2: Is everyone genuinely bad at using AI, or what? I run a very profitable small software company in the US, and our systems routinely handle hundreds of millions in annual transactions, netting over fourteen million dollars monthly. I have not written a single line of code in over a year, because everything gets built solo across two Claude Max plans that I switch between. While critics keep complaining about slop code, the product keeps shipping. Posted from /g/ in October 2026, still profitable.
clips.text_en_c1: Is everyone simply incompetent at leveraging AI? What, in god's name, is the basis for claiming that AI produces nothing but slop? I run a profitable small software firm in the US whose systems process hundreds of millions of dollars in transactions annually, netting comfortably above fourteen million per month. I have not written a line of code in over twelve months. My entire output is built solo, alternating between two Claude Max subscriptions to keep throughput high. Posted from /g/ in October 2026; the venture remains profitable, and I am sleeping extraordinarily well.
clips.text_en_c2: There persists a rather vocal constituency convinced that machine-generated code is inherently slop, a contention with which my own experience is profoundly at odds. I presently work, entirely solo, for a highly profitable American software concern, having architected systems that process transaction volumes measured in the hundreds of millions annually, with monthly profits comfortably clearing fourteen million dollars. I have not personally committed a single line of code to any of these products in over twelve months; my entire development workflow consists of alternating between two Claude Max subscriptions. Whatever the prevailing scepticism may hold, the underlying tooling has proven itself, at least in my hands, remarkably capable. Filed from /g/, October 2026, and the revenue continues to accumulate without intervention.
clips.source_hint: /g/ solo dev claims no code for a year, ships product with two Claude Max plans

clips.text_zh: 有個老豆喺政府工做，搵個仔寫個信用合作社system。佢用Elysia、Solid、Postgres，仲要Nix systemd-nspawn。wtf真係離晒地。
clips.text_en_b1: Dad is now the standard for software engineering. Be me, neet programmer. Dad works at a government union and asks if I can make a system to manage their credit association. It is potentially a huge project, so I try my best: custom SSR framework with Elysia, Solid and Postgres, no third-party services or dependencies, Nix and systemd-nspawn for containers.
clips.text_en_b2: Be me, a neet programmer. Dad works at a government union and casually asks if I can build a system to manage their credit association. Realising the project could easily scale into something massive, I pull out all the stops: a custom SSR framework built on Elysia, Solid and Postgres, with no third-party dependencies whatsoever. Nix and systemd-nspawn handle the containers. Once I see millions flowing through the fund, panic sets in, so I start studying database theory and skimming textbooks for proper procedures.
clips.text_en_c1: My father has effectively become the benchmark for software engineering. Be me, a neet programmer whose dad works at a government union and casually asks whether I might assemble a system to administer their credit association. Given that millions flow through the fund annually, the stakes are rather higher than a weekend hackathon. My stack: a custom SSR framework built on Elysia with Solid and Postgres, zero third-party dependencies whatsoever, and Nix plus systemd-nspawn handling containerisation. I have been poring over database theory textbooks in a cold sweat. The thread was posted on /g/ today and continues accruing replies.
clips.text_en_c2: My father has unwittingly become the benchmark against which all professional software engineering must henceforth be measured. The circumstances were as follows: a neet programmer, myself, prevailed upon by a father employed at a government union to construct a credit-association management system of potentially considerable scope. Recognising the gravity of the undertaking, I deployed a bespoke server-rendered framework built upon Elysia, Solid, and Postgres, eschewing all third-party services and external dependencies; Nix and systemd-nspawn handle the containerisation layer with admirable parsimony. Upon auditing the fund's flow and discovering that millions traverse it annually, I was consumed by an almost primal panic concerning reliability, and promptly immersed myself in database theory to assuage my anxiety.
clips.source_hint: /g/ neet builds gov-union credit system with custom SSR + Postgres

clips.text_zh: Bloomberg話美國70%人paycheck to paycheck，最窮嗰50%只揸2.5%財富。咁我返Florida都係做炮灰。靠AI續命。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Update, as per Bloomberg yesterday. The bottom 40% of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck. However, another 30%, even though with higher income, are also living paycheck to paycheck. The bottom 70% of Americans live paycheck to paycheck. Everyone else has cut back on spending also. Only the upper echelon, the top 5%, are doing well.
clips.text_en_b2: According to Bloomberg yesterday, the bottom forty percent of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck, and another thirty percent with higher incomes are doing the same. That puts roughly seventy percent of the country in the same boat, while everyone else has been forced to cut back. Only the top five percent are genuinely thriving, since the bottom fifty percent own a measly 2.5 percent of total wealth. If you fall outside that top bracket, you are essentially working for tips.
clips.text_en_c1: Update, drawing on Bloomberg figures released yesterday. The bottom forty percent of Americans are demonstrably subsisting paycheck to paycheck, yet the problem does not terminate there: an additional thirty percent, despite materially higher incomes, find themselves in precisely the same predicament. Effectively, the bottom seventy percent are living hand to mouth. The remainder have been compelled to retrench expenditure across the board. Only the upper echelon, broadly the top five percent, are flourishing. As a sobering coda: the bottom fifty percent collectively hold a mere two and a half percent of aggregate wealth. If you fall outside that top five percent, you are fundamentally working for tips.
clips.text_en_c2: Per Bloomberg's most recent dispatch, the macroeconomic picture for the median American household is, if anything, even grimmer than the prevailing consensus suggests. The bottom forty per cent are, predictably, living hand to mouth, but a further thirty per cent of ostensibly higher-earning households find themselves in identical straits, yielding a cumulative seventy per cent of the population subsisting paycheck to paycheck. Even those marginally above this cohort have retrenched aggressively on discretionary expenditure. Only the uppermost five per cent are demonstrably flourishing, a stratification made starker by the observation that the bottom half commands a scarcely believable 2.5 per cent of aggregate wealth. If one falls outside that gilded stratum, one is, functionally speaking, working for gratuities.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ anon summarizes Bloomberg piece on 70% of Americans living paycheck to paycheck

clips.text_en_b2: Wood is supposedly the rarest material in the entire universe, far scarcer than gold or diamonds, which means any invading aliens would come for timber rather than precious metals. clips.text_en_c1: This, ladies and gentlemen, concludes the right-wing investor thesis for good. Wood is, by every meaningful metric, the rarest material in the observable universe, considerably scarcer than gold or diamonds. Should extraterrestrials elect to invade, they would come for lumber, not bullion. Gold, by contrast, is genuinely abundant both throughout the cosmos and within the earth's crust, rendering it effectively worthless. Lumber closed limit up on the CME last Friday. The /biz/ poster closes with the rallying cry 'wood gang for the win', and a handful of anons are purportedly initiating long positions in the November 2026 contract.
clips.text_en_c2: The proposition before us, advanced with characteristic gravitas by an enterprising /biz/ interlocutor, is that timber constitutes the rarest material in the cosmos, eclipsing gold and diamond alike in scarcity. Should an extraterrestrial civilisation harbour designs upon our planetary resources, the argument runs, their interest would be piqued by lumber rather than precious metals; gold, after all, is comparatively abundant throughout the universe and within the Earth's mantle, rendering it effectively worthless. Lumber futures, by contrast, closed limit up on the CME last Friday, and the contrarian thesis is gathering momentum. Several anons have already declared their intention to initiate long positions in the November 2026 contract. Wood gang, it transpires, may yet prevail.

clips.text_zh: 笑死。我gym buddy squat 500磅，但行三層樓梯就chur到震。肥仔信都係咁，一落gym就唔郁。靠AI續命都唔得。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: My gym buddy squats over 500 lbs, but the second we finish lifting, he refuses to do any cardio. He is convinced a 10-minute incline walk will ruin his progress at the end. Today we walked out and had to take some flights of stairs to the upper parking deck because of construction on the lower levels.
clips.text_en_b2: My gym buddy can squat well over 500 pounds, yet the moment we finish lifting, he flat-out refuses any cardio, convinced that a ten-minute incline walk would somehow undo his gains. Today we left the gym and had to climb several flights of stairs to the upper parking deck because construction had closed the lower levels. Halfway up he was already huffing, gripping the rail, and forced to stop after barely three flights. Strong on the squat rack, useless on the stairs.
clips.text_en_c1: My training partner can squat comfortably in excess of 500 pounds, yet the instant we conclude a session, he categorically refuses any cardiovascular work whatsoever. He remains thoroughly convinced that a modest ten-minute incline walk will catastrophically undo whatever gains he has accrued. Today we exited the facility and were obliged to ascend several flights of stairs to the upper parking deck owing to ongoing construction below. By the third flight he was audibly gasping, white-knuckling the handrail, and compelled to slow to a crawl. I struggle to fathom the rationale behind cultivating strength that evaporates the moment a staircase appears. Posted on /fit/ today, October 2026.
clips.text_en_c2: My training partner, whose back squat now exceeds five hundred pounds with apparent ease, exhibits a curious blind spot where cardiovascular exertion is concerned; he maintains, with quasi-religious conviction, that a ten-minute incline walk at the session's conclusion would catastrophically compromise his hard-won gains. The schism between his lower-body prowess and his aerobic capacity was rendered rather vivid this afternoon, when construction in the lower lot compelled us to ascend several flights of stairs to the upper parking deck. He was audibly wheezing by the third landing, clutching the handrail with the desperate resolve of a man confronting mortality, and was obliged to pause repeatedly. The pursuit of raw strength, I maintain, ought not to render one incapable of navigating a staircase.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ anon mocks gym partner who squats heavy but can't do stairs

clips.text_en_c2: Sasaki and Pi-Chan has returned for a second season, and the discourse surrounding it on /a/ is already the customary fevered mixture of anticipation and exasperated resignation. The anime, which premiered on Tokyo MX this October, slots neatly into the now-familiar template of age-gap narratives that resolutely refuse to advance beyond teasing implication, thereby satisfying what has become an almost genre-mandated stipulation that at least one seasonal offering aimed squarely at male audiences must reaffirm the moral propriety of eschewing younger paramours.
